content:
According to 9to5Mac's web traffic analysis, Apple is testing iOS 27.0.1 for iPhone. The update is expected to focus on bug fixes and performance improvements.

iOS 27.0.1 is coming soon

iOS 27.0.1 began appearing in 9to5Mac's analytics data a few days ago. MacRumors also reported the same.

Apple told 9to5Mac this morning that it will release a software update early next week to fix an issue affecting some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models that causes the devices to restart automatically after a failed Face ID authentication.

We reported on this issue earlier this week, explaining that the problem occurs when users attempt to use Face ID to unlock apps such as Passwords. Once Face ID authentication fails, the iPhone may unexpectedly restart.

I was unable to reproduce this issue on my own iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but it is clearly affecting some users. The good news is that this is a software-fixable bug, not any kind of hardware failure.

iOS 27.0.1 will likely address the aforementioned issue (although this has not yet been officially confirmed), and may also include fixes for other bugs in iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.

Have you encountered any issues since updating to iOS 27? What about iPhone 18 Pro-specific problems? Let us know in the comments.
